note: Option normalisation. Upstream is a real Manager built with autoConnect false, read back through its own accessors (reconnection(), reconnectionDelay(), …); the mount path is read from the engine.io Socket the Manager would create, because that is where the trailing slash is added. Times are in milliseconds. `reconnectionAttempts` is null when unlimited, since upstream's default is Infinity, which has no JSON form.

cases.deviation: socket.io-client defaults `reconnection` to TRUE (`opts.reconnection !== false`). A Go struct's zero value cannot express a true default, and Options is part of a published API, so Options.Reconnection stays false-by-default and must be set explicitly. Documented in socket.io/API-DEVIATIONS.md. socket.io-client defaults `randomizationFactor` to 0.5. The same Go zero-value limitation applies: 0 is indistinguishable from unset, so the port leaves reconnection jitter off unless RandomizationFactor is set. Documented in socket.io/API-DEVIATIONS.md.

cases.note: with reconnection set explicitly the only remaining difference is the jitter default
cases.deviation: socket.io-client defaults `randomizationFactor` to 0.5. The same Go zero-value limitation applies: 0 is indistinguishable from unset, so the port leaves reconnection jitter off unless RandomizationFactor is set. Documented in socket.io/API-DEVIATIONS.md.

cases.note: reconnection off and jitter set: everything else must agree exactly
every option set explicitly: no defaulting on either side
a custom initial delay must not disturb the ceiling default
the mount path gains its trailing slash on both sides

cases.deviation: Manager stores randomizationFactor verbatim (1.5) and only backo2 later decides that a value outside (0,1] means no jitter; the port normalises it to 0 up front, at the option layer. The resulting SCHEDULE is identical — see the bo-jitter-over-one case — only the reported option value differs.
